item.title: Weekly roundup: FTC reaches agreement with Stream Auto, UAW wants House China panel kept, Tennessee blocks Scout dealer license
item.dc:creator: CBT News Editorial Team
item.description:
ICYMI: The FTC reached an agreement with Stream Auto Outlet over deceptive vehicle pricing. The UAW is urging Congress to

The post Weekly roundup: FTC reaches agreement with Stream Auto, UAW wants House China panel kept, Tennessee blocks Scout dealer license appeared first on CBT News.
item.content:encoded:
ICYMI: The FTC reached an agreement with Stream Auto Outlet over deceptive vehicle pricing. The UAW is urging Congress to keep the House China Select Committee in place. Tennessee regulators denied Scout Motors a dealer license for direct sales. The average new vehicle price hit a record $51,109 in October. Hertz will close its dedicated car sales locations and focus on online sales.

Here’s a closer look at these top stories and more headlines to keep you up to date on this week’s automotive news.

FTC reaches agreement with Stream Auto Outlet over deceptive vehicle pricing
On Nov. 9, the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) announced an agreement with Stream Auto Outlet, a dealership group based in Long Island, New York, to resolve allegations of misleading vehicle pricing practices. The FTC alleges the dealership advertised prices significantly lower than what consumers ultimately paid. Read more.

UAW urges Congress to keep watching Chinese automakers
The United Auto Workers is urging Congress to keep the House China Select Committee in place when Democrats take control of the chamber, citing concerns about Chinese automakers. The union’s push comes as a permanent ban on Chinese vehicles still hasn’t cleared Congress, and dealers will want to keep an eye on it. Read more.

Tennessee denies Scout Motors dealer license for direct sales
Tennessee regulators have denied Scout Motors a dealer license, preventing the Volkswagen-owned brand from selling directly to buyers in the state for now. According to Kelley Blue Book, the decision is a setback for a brand that plans to sell its Terra truck and Traveler SUV directly rather than through dealerships. Read more.

Average new vehicle price hits record $51,109 in October
According to Kelley Blue Book data, the average new vehicle buyer in the U.S. paid a record $51,109 in October, topping the previous high of $50,614 set last December. Sales of lower-priced compact cars and SUVs are rising, but they aren’t growing fast enough to offset demand for expensive full-size trucks. Read more.

Hertz to close dedicated car sales locations, shift focus to online sales
Hertz is closing its dedicated Hertz Car Sales locations as it focuses its used-vehicle retail strategy on online sales and its rental network. The company confirmed the change in a statement sent to CBT News. Read more.

Next Week: Exclusive Interviews You Can’t Miss 

How Open Road Capital pairs minority equity with operational freedom
For decades, retail automotive succession followed a rigid binary formula of dealer principals either retaining total ownership with all personal net worth tied to the store, or selling the entire operation to a consolidator, forfeiting their family name, employee culture, and local standing. On Monday’s episode of Inside Automotive, we sat down with Open Road Capital Co-Founders Tim Batchelor and Eric Chelline, alongside Operating Partner Jesse Hord of Keeler Motor Car Company, join us to discuss how flexible equity models solve succession challenges, align with manufacturer goals, and fuel multi-state dealership growth. 

Next Week on CBT Live: We’re Live from Used Car Week 2026
Join CBT News Co-Founders Bridget and Jim Fitzpatrick live from Used Car Week in San Diego! We’ll have live updates and interviews from the event every day at noon Eastern (9:00 a.m. PT) Monday through Wednesday. Monday’s guests include Bill Zadeits, President of Cherokee Media Group and Chair of Used Car Week, and Kyle Elder of Street Volkswagen of Amarillo.

item.title: Delivrd’s Tomi Mikula on what dealers get wrong about car buyers
item.dc:creator: Jason Becknell
item.description:
On today’s edition of CBT Live, Tomi Mikula, Founder of Delivrd, joins us to discuss what he hears when he

The post Delivrd’s Tomi Mikula on what dealers get wrong about car buyers appeared first on CBT News.
item.content:encoded:
On today’s edition of CBT Live, Tomi Mikula, Founder of Delivrd, joins us to discuss what he hears when he calls dealerships on behalf of car buyers. A former salesperson and F&I manager with over six years in retail, Mikula started Delivrd four years ago after deciding he couldn’t fix the car buying experience from inside the dealership.

Mikula also answered multiple questions from CBT News viewers, including how shipping works on out-of-state deals, why he asks dealers for out-the-door numbers by text instead of email, and what advice he has for BDC agents.

Sign up for CBT News’ daily newsletter and get the latest industry stories delivered straight to your inbox.

One question Mikula often gets asked is whether he is a broker. Mikula says he’s not a broker, but a customer buying advocate. Brokers typically partner with a set of dealerships and advertise specific inventory and deals from them, he explained, while Delivrd works with buyers and shops each deal individually. He says they get paid whether or not the client buys a car, and clients sign everything directly with the dealership. Mikula said clients can expect their deal to start within 24 to 48 hours of hiring Delivrd and a car in the driveway within five to seven business days.

Mikula said only about 10% to 20% of his calls turn into what he’d call a good experience, even though roughly half of the people he reaches are nice on the phone, and he pointed to the BDC as one of the biggest holdups because callers often hand over their information and then never get the promised callback. He estimates that about 40% of dealers aren’t FTC compliant in one way or another, with 70% to 80% non-compliance in some markets and closer to 95% compliance in others, and he said that includes some of the biggest dealer groups in the country.

For dealers, Mikula said any step that adds resistance to the sale is a mistake. Salespeople should be able to give numbers over the phone and negotiate their own deals, which means training them to hold gross instead of sending every call back to a manager, and every call should be greeted with energy and excitement because the first impression matters so much. He also sees a one-price model as the future of the industry and he sees Delivrd as part of that push.

item.title: AutoNation’s “Drive Pink” program tops $50 million raised for cancer in 10 years
item.dc:creator: Jason Becknell
item.description:
On today’s edition of CBT Live, Ashley Shea, Director of Corporate Affairs at AutoNation, joins us to discuss DRV PNK

The post AutoNation’s “Drive Pink” program tops $50 million raised for cancer in 10 years appeared first on CBT News.
item.content:encoded:
On today’s edition of CBT Live, Ashley Shea, Director of Corporate Affairs at AutoNation, joins us to discuss DRV PNK (Drive Pink), the company’s year-round commitment to drive out cancer. The program is celebrating its 10th anniversary after raising and donating more than $50 million.

DRV PNK began 10 years ago to support breast cancer research. Associates then asked about pediatric cancer, prostate cancer and the cancer centers in their own communities, and the program grew to support efforts to eliminate all cancers. The work still happens at the store level, where leaders run local 5Ks and golf tournaments or buy tables at galas, and the money they raise stays in the community to support local cancer centers and nonprofits, Shea said.

Sign up for CBT News’ daily newsletter and get the latest industry stories delivered straight to your inbox.

To mark the anniversary, AutoNation announced another $1 million in grants to 10 nonprofit partners. That includes $100,000 to the American Cancer Society’s Road to Recovery program, which gets patients to treatment, and $100,000 to the Breast Cancer Research Foundation to fund early career researchers. Funding also goes to Camp Rainbow, a week-long camp for pediatric cancer patients that Phoenix Children’s Hospital puts on and that the donation covers in full.

Store leaders choose what to support, and ideas come from every level of the business, from receptionists and porters to general managers, according to Shea. AutoNation’s 11 market presidents raised $341,000 for the American Cancer Society in October through the Men Wear Pink campaign, using dunk tanks, cookouts and other store events. Customers have joined in too, asking for the pink license plate frames to honor a mom fighting breast cancer or their own survival.

Shea encouraged dealers of any size, from a 100-unit group to a single store, to lean into being part of the community and to keep the door open for employees to say what it needs.

“Just anything that you do is going to make a difference. There’s nothing that’s too small,” Shea said. Any dollar raised or hour volunteered builds a deeper connection to the community and to customers.

item.title: Q3 2026 analysis shows sustained commercial vehicle demand and transaction velocity
item.dc:creator: CBT News Editorial Team
item.description:
Chico, CA—Nov 11, 2026 (GlobeNewswire) – Work Truck Solutions®, the leading commercial vehicle authority, has released its Q3 2026 Commercial

The post Q3 2026 analysis shows sustained commercial vehicle demand and transaction velocity appeared first on CBT News.
item.content:encoded:
Chico, CA—Nov 11, 2026 (GlobeNewswire) – Work Truck Solutions®, the leading commercial vehicle authority, has released its Q3 2026 Commercial Vehicle Market Analysis. Q3 data reveals a commercial vehicle market operating at healthy operational levels. Building on positive fleet replacement signals from Q2, new commercial vehicle sales movement per dealer expanded further even as on-lot availability tightened. Meanwhile, the pre-owned market continues to actively absorb fleet trade-ins, maintaining steady turnover, while increasing in transaction volume.

New Work Truck and Van Market

  • The average final price ($59,635) for new work trucks increased a modest 0.8% Quarter over Quarter (QoQ) and 2.7% Year over Year (YoY).
  • Following a brief Q2 plateau where inventory levels held flat, availability resumed its downward trend in Q3, with average on-lot inventory per dealer falling 3.1% QoQ to 126 units—a 22.2% contraction compared to Q3 2025.
  • Sales (movement) per dealer rose 4.0% QoQ on the heels of Q2’s increase of +8.7, but down 3.7% YoY.
  • Days to Turn (DTT) continued to improve, falling to 167 days, reflecting a 2.9% QoQ decrease and a significant 17.3% decline YoY.

New vehicle availability continues a general downward trend, keeping dealer lots lean. Lean inventory, paired with demand, is accelerating inventory turnover.

Used Work Truck and Van Market

  • The average final price ($37,240) for used commercial vehicles held nearly steady with only a marginal -0.7% QoQ decrease, while remaining 13.3% higher YoY.
  • On-lot used inventory per dealer dipped slightly, down 3.4% QoQ, but up 3.7% YoY.
  • Sales (movement) grew 9.1% QoQ and 9.1% YoY.
  • DTT QoQ numbers remained steady at 56 days, but YoY DTT was up 3.7% compared to the Q3 2025 DTT metric of 54 days.
  • The 2-quarter upward trajectory of used vehicle’s median mileage nearly plateaued, revealing a minor drop of -.2% QoQ, and -1.1% YoY.

A plateau in median mileage shows that fleet managers are again cycling their fleet inventory more readily. Pre-owned work trucks and vans are turning over in under two months, demonstrating strong B2B buyer appetite for affordable operational assets.

New Commercial BEV/PHEV/HEV Market Insights

The average final price for new battery electric (BEV), plugin hybrid electric (PHEV), and hybrid electric (HEV) work trucks reached $65,921, climbing 19.1% Quarter over Quarter—sharply reversing last quarter’s 5.9% dip—and increasing 14.2% Year over Year.

Segment Highlight: Regional Markets

This quarter also includes a new segment spotlight on regional data, where Central, Northeast, South, and West activity revealed several noteworthy shifts in pricing, inventory, and buyer behavior across IHS market regions. Readers can explore the full breakdown, including region-specific trends and insights, in our Q3 2026 Regional Market Analysis.  

Previous highlights were the Q1 Commercial Van Market Analysis and Q2 2026 Duty Classes Market Analysis.

Industry Perspective

“Our Q3 2026 data shows a commercial vehicle market that is running lean in terms of inventory,” said Aaron Johnson, CEO of Work Truck Solutions. “New work truck inventory dipped, yet sales rose for the quarter and days to turn dropped. Commercial buyers are not waiting on the sidelines. As work truck availability remains tight, inventory sourcing tools like our Vehicle Acquisition Search Tool are helping dealers find the work trucks that businesses need, even when they don’t have that specific inventory on-lot.”

Johnson added, “On the pre-owned side, we are seeing sustained momentum from fleet lifecycle rotations. Median mileage has essentially levelled off and sales are up over 9% quarter over quarter, with vehicles continuing to turn quickly. Dealers using targeted digital merchandising to highlight the ongoing reliability and work-readiness of these pre-owned work trucks and vans are capitalizing.”

It’s important to note that these datasets include multiple subsets averaged within the segments and don’t necessarily reflect the individual dynamics of each subset. For instance, in the “New Work Trucks and Vans” dataset, the average price came in at $59, 635, but each subset has its own average; e.g., Service Trucks averaged $64,484 while Box Trucks averaged $51,812 and Stripped Chassis averaged $43,774. The same is true for all segments: Price, Inventory, DTT, Sales, and Mileage.

About Work Truck Solutions

Work Truck Solutions is the industry’s platform and operating system that enables all stakeholders in the ecosystem—class 1-8 dealers, OEMs, upfitters, and distributors—to efficiently serve the businesses and fleet managers who need work trucks and vans. With innovative solutions supporting the vehicle sales life cycle through customer relationship management, inventory management, operational analytics, digital marketing and supply chain optimization, Work Truck Solutions helps those in the work truck and van space, no matter their role in the supply chain, by providing increased visibility and efficiency so that all businesses can focus on doing their jobs.

item.title: Stellantis names new chief commercial officer over U.S. sales and dealer network
item.dc:creator: Jason Becknell
item.description:
On the Dash: Stellantis chief commercial officer Tim Kuniskis now oversees U.S. retail, fleet sales and the dealer network. Michael

The post Stellantis names new chief commercial officer over U.S. sales and dealer network appeared first on CBT News.
item.content:encoded:
On the Dash:

  • Stellantis chief commercial officer Tim Kuniskis now oversees U.S. retail, fleet sales and the dealer network.
  • Michael Orange left after less than seven months as senior vice president of U.S. sales.
  • Bob Broderdorf returns to lead Dodge, and Matt McAlear now focuses only on Chrysler.

Stellantis dealers now have one executive overseeing brands, marketing, retail and fleet sales, and the dealer network. The automaker named Tim Kuniskis its U.S. chief commercial officer. The move adds sales and network responsibilities to his role as head of the company’s American brands. The announcement came just over a week after Stellantis named a new North America chief operating officer.

The change comes with the departure of Michael Orange, who joined Stellantis in April as senior vice president of U.S. sales and network performance. Stellantis also made leadership moves at Dodge and Chrysler. Kuniskis will report to Pablo Di Si, the company’s North America COO.

Sign up for CBT News’ daily newsletter and get the latest industry stories delivered straight to your inbox.

Kuniskis adds U.S. retail, fleet and dealer network

Kuniskis already led Stellantis’ American brands, the SRT performance division, and North America marketing and retail strategy, a job he took in July 2025. With the new title he also takes on U.S. retail sales, fleet sales and the dealer network. He reports directly to Di Si.

Kuniskis joined the company in 1992 and has run Dodge, Jeep, Alfa Romeo, Maserati and Ram over the years. He announced his retirement in May 2024 and came back the following summer. Matt VanDyke succeeded him as Ram CEO in July.

Di Si said bringing brands, marketing, the dealer network and sales strategy together creates “a clear line of decision-making.” He added that Kuniskis knows the brands, the customers and the company well, and tied the structure to the aggressive targets in the FaSTLAne 2030 strategic plan.

Orange leaves after less than seven months

Stellantis hired Orange from Hyundai Motor America, where he was vice president of national sales, to lead U.S. sales and network performance. He started April 22 and reported to CEO Antonio Filosa, taking over from Jeff Kommor, who was retiring after 40 years of service.

Orange came with deep experience that included time at Nissan North America and Wells Fargo Auto Finance. The job centered on strengthening retail performance, dealer partnerships and market share growth.

The top U.S. sales seat has now changed hands twice in about seven months, first from Kommor to Orange and now from Orange to Kuniskis. Orange has left the company, Stellantis said.

More leadership changes for Stellantis brands

Bob Broderdorf is coming back from medical leave to lead the Dodge brand. He had run Jeep since February 2025, and Branden Coté succeeded him there effective Aug. 3, after Stellantis announced the change July 20.

Matt McAlear, who has been Dodge CEO since June 2024, will now focus exclusively on Chrysler. Both brand leaders report to Kuniskis. FaSTLAne 2030 is the five-year strategic plan Stellantis unveiled at its May 2026 Investor Day.

For Stellantis dealers, the dealer network, retail and fleet sales, marketing and the American brands now sit under Kuniskis. He reports directly to Di Si, who took over North America operations in early November. The Dodge and Chrysler leaders report to Kuniskis as well.

The post Stellantis names new chief commercial officer over U.S. sales and dealer network appeared first on CBT News.

item.title: Federal judge sides with CDK Global on Tekion’s monopoly claims
item.dc:creator: Jason Becknell
item.description:
On the Dash: CDK Global won summary judgment on Tekion’s monopolization and attempted monopolization claims. The court found CDK’s share

The post Federal judge sides with CDK Global on Tekion’s monopoly claims appeared first on CBT News.
item.content:encoded:
On the Dash:

  • CDK Global won summary judgment on Tekion’s monopolization and attempted monopolization claims.
  • The court found CDK’s share stayed below 50% in 2023 and 2024 while Tekion kept growing.
  • The order is partial and covers only the two antitrust counts CDK asked about.

A federal judge has ruled for CDK Global on the central antitrust claims in its fight with rival Tekion, finding that no reasonable jury could conclude CDK held monopoly power in the dealer management system market. U.S. District Judge Jacqueline Scott Corley granted CDK summary judgment on Tekion’s monopolization and attempted monopolization claims in an order filed Nov. 10.

The order doesn’t settle every dispute between the two companies, though. It covers only the two antitrust counts CDK asked the court to decide, and it came after oral argument on Oct. 22. Tekion sued CDK in December 2024, and the fight since then has included a data access dispute, a countersuit and several court rulings.

Sign up for CBT News’ daily newsletter and get the latest industry stories delivered straight to your inbox.

Court finds CDK’s share fell below 50% as Tekion grew

The court found no genuine dispute that CDK’s share of the U.S. franchise dealer DMS market was below 50% in 2023 and 2024, whether measured by dealership locations or by revenue. CDK said its share of locations peaked at 42.3% at the end of 2022 and fell to 36.4% by March 2026. Tekion had argued that CDK held 50% to 60% of the market, but the judge found its evidence was outdated.

In her Nov. 10 order, Judge Jacqueline Scott Corley said, “The available evidence does not support a finding that CDK possessed monopoly power during the relevant time period or was dangerously close to obtaining such powers.”

Tekion grew and won customers from CDK throughout the period, including Asbury Automotive Group, and its DMS revenue more than doubled between 2023 and 2024. Judge Corley also denied Tekion’s request for more discovery and excluded its expert’s revenue share estimate as unreliable. Because CDK’s share was falling, she found no dangerous probability that it would gain monopoly power.

How the Tekion and CDK dispute reached this point

Tekion filed its federal antitrust lawsuit in December 2024, accusing CDK of using anticompetitive tactics to keep dealers on its platform and of holding dealer data hostage. Tekion asked for damages and an injunction that would force CDK to move dealer data right away.

The suit followed a data fight over Asbury Automotive Group, when a court ordered CDK to hand over data from Asbury dealerships to Tekion after CDK initially resisted. CDK countersued Tekion in February 2025, alleging Tekion illegally accessed confidential dealer data to win business. Tekion denied the claims and called the suit without merit. Judge Corley let Tekion’s case move forward in July 2025, when she denied CDK’s motion to dismiss.

The post Federal judge sides with CDK Global on Tekion’s monopoly claims appeared first on CBT News.

item.title: Honda’s top-selling CR-V to go 100% hybrid next year
item.dc:creator: Jason Becknell
item.description:
On the Dash: Honda CR-V goes 100% hybrid with the 2028 model arriving next year. Hybrids make up over 50%

The post Honda’s top-selling CR-V to go 100% hybrid next year appeared first on CBT News.
item.content:encoded:
On the Dash:
  • Honda CR-V goes 100% hybrid with the 2028 model arriving next year.
  • Hybrids make up over 50% of CR-V sales as the SUV nears 400,000 units.
  • The new two-motor hybrid system targets fuel efficiency gains of more than 10%.

Honda is taking its best-selling vehicle fully hybrid. The next-generation 2028 Honda CR-V arrives next year with a new platform, a new two-motor hybrid powertrain and a new design, the company announced in a press release. It’s the seventh generation of the SUV and the first of several hybrid models Honda has confirmed in development for North America by 2030. Honda didn’t share any images of the new CR-V, posting only a teaser of the SUV’s updated logo.

The CR-V is on pace to surpass 400,000 units for the third straight year, and Honda says hybrids account for over 50% of the model’s sales mix. Annual CR-V hybrid sales have grown nearly tenfold since the hybrid launched in 2020.

Sign up for CBT News’ daily newsletter and get the latest industry stories delivered straight to your inbox.

The 2028 CR-V will run exclusively on the fifth generation of Honda’s two-motor hybrid system, which Honda says increases the standard power and efficiency of the SUV. Honda is aiming to improve fuel efficiency by more than 10%, and the system adds a newly developed electric AWD unit for precise, responsive motor control. The new platform combines high body rigidity with light weight and a modular architecture that allows greater parts commonality.

Honda says the CR-V is America’s all-time best-selling SUV, with more than 7.5 million units sold, and the best-selling light-duty vehicle in the U.S. through October 2026. It’s been Honda’s best-selling vehicle every year since 2017, and 2027 marks its 30th anniversary. Luis Guerra, assistant vice president of Honda National Auto Sales, said the 100% hybrid powertrain will further expand the SUV’s appeal as demand for hybrid-electric vehicles reaches record levels.

Production stays in North America. The new hybrid power unit will be built at the Honda Transmission Plant in Ohio, where hybrid system capacity is set to increase 250% in the coming years, and the Anna Engine Plant is retooling a line for the next-generation four-cylinder Atkinson-cycle engine. The CR-V will continue to be built at the East Liberty Auto Plant in Ohio, the Indiana Auto Plant and Honda of Canada Mfg.

For dealers, hybrids now represent about 30% of all Honda brand sales. Honda set back-to-back hybrid sales records in 2024 and 2025 and is on track for another record year in 2026, and it says hybrid and SUV consideration are at all-time highs.

item.title: Ford bringing back the Mustang Cobra for 2027, hints at a Cobra R
item.dc:creator: Jason Becknell
item.description:
On the Dash: Mustang Cobra returns in 2027 after a gap since the 2004 model year, Ford Racing confirmed. Ford’s

The post Ford bringing back the Mustang Cobra for 2027, hints at a Cobra R appeared first on CBT News.
item.content:encoded:
On the Dash:

  • Mustang Cobra returns in 2027 after a gap since the 2004 model year, Ford Racing confirmed.
  • Ford’s teaser ends with the R in Cobra highlighted in blue, hinting at a Cobra R.
  • Ford hasn’t shared specs, pricing or a reveal date for either model.

Ford is bringing the Mustang Cobra back in 2027, and the teaser video it released this week hints that a Cobra R could be coming along with it. The Cobra name hasn’t appeared on a Mustang since the 2004 model year, so the announcement is a big moment for the performance side of the lineup.

Ford Racing posted the teaser on Instagram on Nov. 10, and it features the sound of a V8 climbing through the gears while the word “Cobra” spells out on screen. The caption promises an “all-motor heart born from racing” and says the story continues in 2027, language that suggests a naturally aspirated engine, according to Ford Racing.

Sign up for CBT News’ daily newsletter and get the latest industry stories delivered straight to your inbox.

Here’s the teaser Ford Racing posted on Instagram, with the Cobra logo and the V8 sound that has fans talking. The video ends with the letter R in “Cobra” highlighted in blue, and that’s where the Cobra R speculation comes from.

 

View this post on Instagram

 

A post shared by Ford Racing (@fordracing)

Ford hasn’t confirmed a Cobra R, and it hasn’t shared specs, pricing or a reveal date beyond 2027. It also hasn’t said whether the Cobra will be its own model or a new addition to the current Mustang lineup.

The original Mustang Cobra R was a limited-production, track-focused car offered in 1993, 1995 and 2000, with 657 units built in total. Those cars cut weight and added track-tuned suspension, bigger brakes and unique wheels and aero, and today they’re highly collectible.

For Ford dealers, a Cobra and a possible Cobra R give stores another halo performance model to talk about with enthusiast customers well before the cars arrive. It’s a good time to start tracking customer interest and allocation questions, since Ford hasn’t said how many of either model it plans to build.

The post Ford bringing back the Mustang Cobra for 2027, hints at a Cobra R appeared first on CBT News.
